SONA 2015

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A horrified nation watched as armed police bundled the EFF out of the national assembly. What does it mean for our democracy

Summary:
After the chaos at the SONA on Thursday we ask what does it mean for our democracy.

Further information:
SONA 2015 SCRIPT

Commentary One
The prelude to the SONA on Thursday began with the usual pageantry deserving of such an occasion

Up sound brass bands

Commentary one continues
But an undercurrent rippled beneath this pomp- would the EFF follow through with their threat, and once again ask the president to pay back the money.

John Link
Things got off to a rocky start when journalists protested the jamming of the cell phone signal

The jamming would have been illegal under the circumstances

Journo’s chant: bring back the signal, bring back the signal,

Professor Tinyiko Maluleke Political analyst

It is quite astounding – the sheer audacity to do it

Commentary Two
University of Pretoria Professor Tinyiko Maluleke couldn’t believe what he was seeing.

Professor Tinyiko
Whether they were switched back on or not is now no longer relevant, the fact that the signals were switched off tells me there are intentions at least in some quarters that we need to be very afraid and worried about.

Commentary Three
With the signal restored the address began

Up sound president speaks

My Fellow South Africans



Commentary Four
But the calm was momentary, soon EFF Godrich Gardee got straight to the point.

Up sound Baleka
Honourable president, honourable president…

Godrich Gardee
Are you going to pay by EFT, cash or e wallet? Thank you!

Bongani
Was the EFF correct in raising the issue the way they did?

Tinyiko
It was inexcusable. No one has a right to do that because there is a value in ritual, so to try and prevent that it is seriously disrespectful, not just of the president but of the nation

Link
In her interview with us last week, the speaker flatly rejected the idea that she protects the president at all costs

Up sound Baleka
Baleka
I reject that! I work according to the rules and I will continue to do that

LINK CONTINUES
But this week as soon as the EFF began to ask the president when he would pay back the money, she called in the heavies to remove them

Commentary five
Parliaments cameras focused on the speaker as the men in white shirts now confirmed as public order police tackled EFF MP’s

Up sound shouting

Commentary six
The showdown we had feared, began to unfold in front of two former presidents international guests and a horrified nation



Professor Tinyiko
What I am not sure about is whether to remove them violently to jam the signals is a kind of response parliament should have for an action like this. It seems to me they wanted to remove a fly they used a hammer and they smashed the forehead of the SA nation with it

Julius Malema outside parliament
We have seen that we are part of a police state where people are unable to give political answers and political solutions they resort to security apparatus

Commentary Seven
All sides say they are working according to the rules. But there is no accountability, making a mockery of parliament according to Business day Editor Songezo Zibi

Songezo
Legally parliament can summons a president to appear before it but we don’t have a parliament Bongani! That institution is a joke! We can blame the speaker all we want – she is merely a passenger in a train going in its own direction

Commentary eight
On Friday Gardee outlined how he believes the situation could have been diffused.

Godrich
What the speaker should have done is said Mr President do you want to answer, if he said no I will answer after the speech or in March that would have disarmed us…the rules say she must do

Songezo
The credibility of parliament is gone – what we are going to see is a deadlock and the EFF and the DA are going to take their fight to the streets

Godrich Gardee
Well if you close the space of democratic expression of peoples opinion in the chamber you are actually saying people should go to the bush and take up arms.



Commentary nine
With the EFF bundled out of the chamber, inside, the president began to chuckle

Up sound president he! He! He!

Songezo
Nobody won – the EFF didn’t – the president didn’t. He was shocking – The first thing he did after the disturbance was to laugh – I wouldn’t laugh it was not funny, and the country lost

Tinyiko
It’s just not the kind of acknowledgment South Africans were expecting. A South African was expecting the president to stand up and say, fellow South Africans I am sorry for what you have just witnessed. This is not what parliament is all about

Bongani
Is this our humpty dumpty moment or can we put it all back together again
Songezo
We are not going to put it together again because it’s the new normal –we better get used to this Bongani everyone we will wait for the next one where even worse happens

Commentary ten
Worse came when UDM’s Bantu Holomisa disgusted by what he had seen, left the house

Bantu Holomisa
I wont be part of a police state! We were threatened here with people carrying guns.

Commentary eleven
He was followed shortly afterwards by the DA

Up sound journo’s scramble outside

Spoilt for choice journalists scrambled from one story to another outside parliament

Mmusi Maimane outside the NA
Look what happened today is a violation of the separation of powers



Professor Tinyiko Maluleke
I think we are in trouble, such is the importance of parliament… has oversight – at least it is independent of the executive and I am not so sure that what we saw does not begin to destroy the separation between parliament and the executive

Commentary twelve
When finally the president did deliver his speech, attention was elsewhere

Tinyiko Maluleke
The SONA occurred when the signal was jammed. When members of the EFF were violently evicted from parliament, that is the moment.– anything else could not match those moments

John Link
By Friday many politicians and ordinary South Africans had condemned what happened in parliament but for the ANC the behavior of the security personnel was not an aberration it was entirely appropriate

Commentary Thirteen
The ANC deputy chief whip blamed a DA, EFF Alliance

Dorris Dlakude
The disgraceful antics of the EFF and the DA which were displayed for the eyes of the entire nation and the international community during an important occasion were designed to not only embarrass the governing party but the entire nation

Commentary Fourteen
An unrepentant and defiant Julius Malema said: We are waiting for him again. Every time he comes here he must fetch those 100 people

Commentary Fifteen
At the DA press conference Mmusi Maimane called for the removal of the speaker for ordering armed police into the house

Mmusi
We believe it was a direct order of the speaker and the NCOP

Commentary Sixteen
Thursday was a well-planned military operation he said

Mmusi
We have very strong information that public order policing were deployed from all over the country to come down for the state of the nation address

Commentary fourteen
Today City Press and Africa Check revealed that it was indeed Public order police that stormed into the chamber in disguise
But the fighting hasnt Baleka declared Malema a cockroach, and the presidency denied they knew about plans to jam the signal

Bongani
Is this a watershed moment
Professor Tinyiko
I hope it is a water-shed moment but I am hesitant because we have had so many turning points and we did not turn, but turning back turning where I hope we are turning back to the integrity of parliament.

THE END 09 05

PROMO ONE
This week the EFF made good on their promise to disrupt the state of the nation address

Tinyiko
There is absolutely no way to excuse the disruption of a ceremony.


PROMO TWO
As the EFF disrupted the presidents state of the nation address police stormed parliament to kick them out and the DA left the house in protest what does all of this mean for our democracy.


















Expert:
Mr. Songezo Zibi
Prof. Tinyiko Maluleke
